judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the identical Grade 2 / Term 3 / Reading and Phonics / 'Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes:' path (same resolved coordinate rank 2, same printed table row 3, page 97), and both address consonant letter-patterns within words: 'Uses consonant blends to build up and break down words' versus 'Recognises common double consonants such as ll, ss and zz) at the end of words'. The shared LC tag 'phonics' plus the complementary LC content (building/breaking words with blends vs. recognising double-consonant word endings) shows substantive conceptual coherence in word-level decoding and encoding. However, they target different phonic elements (blends versus double final consonants) at the same Grade and the same Term, and neither statement's text indicates that proficiency in one is needed for, or substantively extends into, the other; there is no expanded capability or increased complexity to justify a developmental direction, and same-rank/same-term direction requires substantive evidence that is absent. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), but the full printed statements and LCs supplied are sufficient for this symmetric conclusion.

The shared tokens ('story', 'shared') and LC overlap reflect this genuine topical link rather than mere wording repetition. However, neither statement's evidence shows that proficiency in picture-based prediction is needed for, or developmentally extends into, contributing ideas in Shared Writing within the same term; they are complementary same-term activities, so a directional buildsTowards is not supported. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so deeper developmental claims cannot be verified from this bounded excerpt.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 3 (rank 3) of the same CAPS framework but in different skill areas and terms: the first is Term 2 Listening and Speaking (Oral), 'Tells a short story with a simple plot and different characters' (LC tags: plot, characters, storytelling, oral); the second is Term 4 Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading, 'Reads written texts as a whole class with the teacher (shared reading) and discusses characters, the ‘problem’ in the story, the plot and the values in the text' (LCs: shared reading; discusses characters, problem, plot, values). The shared substance is narrative-structure knowledge (plot, characters), not merely repeated wording: command of plot and character in one's own oral storytelling supports the later, more demanding task of analysing and discussing those same narrative elements in a teacher-led written text, where the demand is extended to the story 'problem' and the values in the text. Direction is Term 2 to Term 4 within Grade 3, which is a permitted earlier-to-later direction. Confidence is moderate because the two statements are in different skill areas and the dependency is supportive rather than prerequisite, and both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so full source context could not be inspected.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the same resolved coordinate (Grade 1, rank 1) under Term 2 / WRITING / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' and come from the same Term 2 writing table (page 70, window 19), so no cross-term ordering is involved and direction must rest on substantive content. 'Contributes ideas for a class story (Shared Writing)' (second) is a teacher-scaffolded, collectively composed activity where the learner supplies oral ideas that an adult records; 'Writes one sentence of own news or shared writing' (first) requires the learner to independently commit a composed sentence to paper. Proficiency in generating and shaping ideas in the supported shared-writing context plausibly supports success at producing one's own written sentence, so the developmental direction runs second_to_first within the same term. The pair shares only generic LC tokens ('shared', 'writing'), but the substantive scaffolded-to-independent composition relationship, not the token overlap, grounds this judgment; the direction within a single term is a reasoned inference and carries moderate confidence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all hierarchy nodes carry upstream merge/audit context, which limits certainty without changing the plain statement texts.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Writing, the first under Term 2 / sub-strand 'Emergent Writing' ('Understands that writing and drawing are different and begins to copy letters and numerals ... pretend writing using a mixture of copied letters and squiggles'), the second under Term 3 / sub-strand 'Emergent Handwriting' ('Develops large muscle control: works in pairs or on own to form letters with their bodies'). Term 2 to Term 3 would permit a forward buildsTowards, but the evidence shows two complementary emergent-writing strands rather than a developmental dependency: one is print-awareness and pretend/copying writing with a pencil, the other is gross-motor whole-body letter formation that is a parallel preparatory handwriting activity, not an extension or deepening of pretend writing. Shared tokens ('letters', 'own') and the single shared LC tag 'emergent' are weak lexical/tag overlap, and the only hierarchy signal is the shared Grade R grouping, which alone is not semantic evidence. Meaningful coherence around forming and reproducing letter shapes in Grade R emergent writing supports relatesTo. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so additional context may exist that is not visible here.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 3 (rank 3) and concern applying phonic knowledge to produce words, but in different Skill Areas and Terms: the first is Term 3 / Reading and Phonics / 'Phonic Activities ... 15 minutes' ('Builds words using the phonic skills taught this year'), the second is Term 1 / Writing / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Uses phonic knowledge and spelling rules to write unfamiliar words'). The coherence is substantive and pair-specific — phonics-based word building and phonics/spelling-rule-based encoding of unfamiliar words reinforce one another across the reading-phonics and writing programmes — but the evidence does not show one as a substantive extension, deepening, or increased-complexity successor of the other. The pedagogically natural support direction (phonic word building supporting spelling of unfamiliar words in writing) would run Term 3 to Term 1 within the same Grade, which is not an admissible developmental direction; selecting the reverse direction merely to satisfy term ordering would not be evidence-grounded. Canonical symmetric relatesTo therefore records the meaningful reinforcement without asserting dependency or sequence. Shared LC tags ('phonics', 'spelling') and token/trigram overlap were treated as nomination signals only, not as semantic proof. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (Grade 3 and Term banners were merged nodes), so this judgment is inferred from the excerpted statements and identity scopes.
